t.7.68.1: Long ago, in the Tretā age, there was a forest of vast extent, stretching a hundred yojanas on every side, empty of beasts and bereft of birds.
t.7.68.3: He was indeed unable to describe the beauty of that forest, with its fruits and roots of pleasant taste and its trees of many forms.
t.7.68.2: Performing the highest austerities in that uninhabited forest, O gentle one, I came to that forest in order to traverse it.
t.7.68.4: In the middle of that forest there was a lake a yojana in length, thickly strewn with lotuses and water-lilies and free of moss.
t.7.68.6: Near that lake there was a great and wondrous hermitage, ancient and exceedingly holy, yet empty of ascetics.
t.7.68.5: It was exceedingly wondrous, as it were, its water supremely sweet to taste, free of dust and unruffled, and thronged with splendid flocks of birds.
t.7.68.7: There I spent a summer night, O bull among men; at daybreak, rising early, I set out toward that lake.
t.7.68.8: Then, O king, I saw there in that lake a corpse, well-nourished and unaged, lying somewhere in it, resplendent with supreme beauty.
t.7.68.9: Pondering that matter, O Rāghava, I stood there for a moment on the bank of the lake, wondering, O lord, “What could this possibly be?”
t.7.68.10: Then, after a moment, I saw a celestial vehicle, wondrous to behold and supremely magnificent, yoked with swans and swift as thought.
t.7.68.12: Then, O Rāma, while I looked on, that heaven-dweller descended from his celestial chariot and devoured that corpse, O Raghunandana.
t.7.68.11: There in the celestial chariot, O delight of the Raghus, O hero, a thousand apsarases adorned with divine ornaments wait devotedly upon that dweller of heaven; some sing delightful songs, and others likewise play upon instruments.
t.7.68.13: Then, having eaten his fill of flesh, abundantly and with relish, the heavenly being went down into the lake and began to touch its waters.
t.7.68.14: Having sipped water according to the prescribed rule, that heavenly being, O bull among men, set about mounting the finest and most excellent of celestial chariots.
t.7.68.15: Seeing him, godlike in appearance, ascending, I then spoke these words to him, O bull among men.
t.7.68.16: Who are you, who look like a god? And this food is despised; for what reason is it eaten by you, O gentle one? Please tell me.
t.7.68.17: It is a wonder that so radiant a state, esteemed by the gods, should go with such contemptible food, gentle one; I wish to hear the truth of it.
